strengths: Compelling and timely approach: By shifting from discrete RVQ tokens to continuous VAE latents paired with a consistency head, the paper directly addresses the efficiency and fidelity bottleneck inherent to multi-codebook autoregressive audio models.

Strong empirical results across two domains: The proposed method demonstrates clear improvements over strong RQ-Transformer baselines in both speech and music continuation, supported by both objective metrics (MOSNet, ABX, FAD, PPX, VERT) and rigorous human evaluations (Bayesian Elo ratings).

Effective architectural innovations: The combination of noisy long-term context with a clean short-term context transformer elegantly resolves the error accumulation and detail loss problems in continuous autoregressive music generation.

Practical training and inference enhancements: The head batch multiplier provides significant training speedups and stability by reusing backbone representations across multiple diffusion timesteps, while the Gaussian temperature heuristic offers an effective way to steer diversity in consistency models.

Significant inference acceleration: Replaces slow iterative diffusion sampling with 1-to-4 step consistency modeling, achieving up to 19.3x sampler speedup and ~2x overall generation speedup compared to an RQ-Transformer baseline while preserving high fidelity.
weaknesses: Architectural discrepancy between tasks: Key architectural elements (noise injection into long-term context and the short-context transformer) are vital for music, but omitted for speech because no gain was observed. While this is pragmatic, it highlights domain-specific divergence and leaves open questions about the universality of the proposed design.

Heuristic nature of temperature sampling: The proposed Gaussian temperature sampling adjusts only the noise variance 1/sqrt(tau) and discards the intractable Jacobian determinant term. While the empirical speaker similarity trends in Figure 3 are convincing, further discussion or analysis of potential distributional distortion is warranted.

Direct comparison to related continuous audio baselines: While the ablation study includes a configuration approximating MAR/Pasini et al., the paper would benefit from a more direct empirical comparison with recent continuous speech/audio models (e.g., DiTAR, SALAD) on standard benchmarks.
Minor presentation omission: In the abstract, the audio sample link sentence ends abruptly ('Samples are available at ').

strengths: Compelling and timely direction: addressing the major computational bottleneck and fidelity loss of Residual Vector Quantization (RVQ) discrete audio language models by modeling continuous latents autoregressively.

Effective integration of continuous consistency modeling into the autoregressive framework, enabling 1-step to 4-step sampling and achieving a 12x–20x speedup in the sampling head compared to RQ-Transformers while outperforming 100-step TrigFlow diffusion at low step budgets.

Well-designed technical solutions for continuous autoregressive modeling challenges, notably: (1) pairing noisy long-context conditioning with a clean short-context transformer to combat error accumulation while retaining fine acoustic detail; (2) the head batch multiplier to amortize backbone computation; and (3) a practical Gaussian temperature sampling heuristic.

Comprehensive empirical validation across two distinct audio domains (speech and music continuation), evaluated with both objective benchmarks (FAD, MOSNet, ABX, PPX, VERT) and rigorous human perceptual studies (MOS acoustic quality and Bayesian Elo ratings).
Clear ablation study (Table 5 and Figure 2) validating the impact and necessity of the core design decisions.
weaknesses: Architectural asymmetry across domains: The short-context transformer and noise augmentation were crucial for music generation (Table 5), yet omitted entirely for speech continuation without extensive analysis. While Section 5.1 hypothesizes that the inner monologue text stream serves as a stabilizing semantic anchor, a more thorough ablation/discussion on why speech behaves differently would clarify the generality of the dual-transformer design.

Theoretical depth for Gaussian temperature sampling: The paper observes that sampling noise with variance scaled by temperature improves diversity and metrics, but acknowledges that the Jacobian term in the density transformation is intractable. Treating noise variance scaling as temperature sampling is an empirical heuristic that merits deeper theoretical analysis or comparison to other continuous truncation/sampling techniques.

Missing audio sample link: The abstract ends with an incomplete sentence ('Samples are available at '), omitting the audio demonstration link, which is important for evaluating audio generative models.

strengths: Timely and significant paradigm shift: Bypassing discrete residual vector quantization (RVQ) in favor of autoregressive modeling over continuous VAE latents addresses fundamental bottlenecks in current audio language models (e.g., codebook collapse, quantization loss, and complex token interleaving/flattening schemes).

Novel and effective integration of consistency modeling: Adapting continuous-time consistency models to continuous autoregressive sequence modeling overcomes the major limitation of diffusion-based heads (such as MAR), enabling high-fidelity 1- to 4-step generation and providing a 12× to 19× speedup in the sampling head.

Well-motivated architectural design: The combination of noisy long-term context (to prevent error accumulation) and clean short-context modeling (to preserve fine-grained local details) is conceptually clean and empirically validated via rigorous ablation experiments.

Practical training and sampling innovations: The head batch multiplier provides a simple yet effective strategy to amortize the backbone transformer compute, substantially accelerating training convergence. The Gaussian temperature sampling heuristic effectively bridges a key operational gap between discrete and continuous generative models.

Thorough empirical validation: The framework is demonstrated on both speech continuation (with semantic grounding via inner monologue) and complex long-context music continuation. Evaluations include standard objective metrics (FAD, PPX, VERT, ViSQOL, SI-SNR), human evaluations (MOS and Bayesian Bradley-Terry Elo ratings with confidence intervals), scalability analysis, and component ablations.
weaknesses: Discrepancy between speech and music configurations: The short-context transformer and noise augmentation are central technical contributions for music, yet they are omitted in the speech continuation setup because no gains were observed. The manuscript would benefit from a deeper conceptual analysis explaining why textual inner monologue grounding obviates the need for these mechanisms in speech.

Heuristic nature of temperature sampling: The Gaussian temperature mechanism is purely empirical; the intractable Jacobian determinant is simply omitted. While shown to correlate well with speaker diversity in Figure 3, a more rigorous discussion of its theoretical implications on the implied density would strengthen the paper.

Ammortized system-level speedup: While the sampler head speedup is substantial (12× to 19×), the overall end-to-end speedup is more modest (1.3× to 2.2×) because execution time remains heavily dominated by the autoregressive backbone transformer.

Missing audio demo link: The abstract ends with an incomplete sentence ('Samples are available at '), which was likely left blank for anonymization or as an oversight, but makes qualitative audio verification difficult during review.

strengths: Compelling paradigm shift: The paper provides a well-motivated and effective alternative to discrete RVQ-based audio language models by modeling continuous VAE latents with consistency heads, substantially cutting autoregressive sampling latency.

Comprehensive empirical scope: The proposed framework is evaluated across four diverse audio generation domains (speech continuation, zero-shot TTS, music continuation, and text-to-music), demonstrating broad applicability.

Practical innovations and efficiency: Key design choices—including the dual-stream clean short-context / noisy long-context design, head batch multiplier, latent CFG distillation, and Gaussian temperature sampling—provide significant practical speedups (up to 19x for the sampling head and 2.2x end-to-end) culminating in a 100M TTS model capable of running faster than real-time on CPU.

Rigorous evaluation: The paper complements standard objective metrics (FAD, WER, CER, PPX) with extensive listening tests (MUSHRA and Bayesian Bradley-Terry Elo rankings with confidence intervals), demonstrating competitive or superior perceptual quality compared to strong discrete baselines.
weaknesses: Domain-dependent architectural choices: While the combination of noisy long-term context and clean short-term context is highlighted as essential for music generation (Table 5), it is completely omitted for speech continuation and TTS (as noted in Section 5.1 and Table 14). A deeper theoretical or empirical explanation for why speech does not suffer from error accumulation in the same way as music would strengthen the narrative.

Degradation in objective speaker similarity: In the zero-shot TTS benchmark (Table 3), CALM exhibits a noticeable drop in objective WavLM speaker similarity (0.52 vs. 0.66–0.67 for baselines). Although partially explained by the VAE bottleneck (which itself achieves 0.57), this indicates that the continuous latent space may lose subtle acoustic speaker characteristics.

Missing ablation details on distillation: While latent distillation is key to the efficiency of Pocket TTS (compressing 24 layers to 6 layers and eliminating CFG batch doubling), the paper lacks a detailed quantitative ablation comparing the distilled student directly against the teacher across quality and intelligibility metrics.

Minor presentation issues: The paper contains unanonymized placeholders and formatting gaps (e.g., missing URLs in the abstract and Section 1, and 'Placeholder Author and Various Contributors' in the references).

strengths: Addresses a fundamental computational bottleneck in audio language models by replacing discrete RVQ hierarchies and multi-step diffusion heads with single/few-step continuous consistency models over continuous VAE latents.
Broad empirical validation spanning four distinct generative tasks: speech continuation, text-to-speech (TTS), music continuation, and text-to-music.

Comprehensive evaluation combining standardized objective metrics (WER, CER, FAD, PPX, VERT) with well-designed human perceptual evaluations (Bayesian Elo ratings and MUSHRA tests with confidence intervals).

Introduces effective architectural and engineering enhancements, such as the head batch multiplier (amortizing heavy backbone forward passes across multiple noise levels), the hybrid noisy long-term / clean short-context conditioning, and latent distillation for edge deployment.

Strong practical impact demonstrated by 'Pocket TTS'—a distilled 100M-parameter model achieving low WER, strong human audio quality ratings, and faster-than-real-time generation on standard laptop CPUs.

Thorough ablation studies verifying the necessity of each component (e.g., head batch multiplier, noise injection, short-context transformer, and trade-offs between TrigFlow and consistency modeling).
weaknesses: Architectural inconsistency across modalities: while the dual-context design (noise injection + short-context transformer) is shown to be critical for music continuation (Table 5), it provided no benefit and was omitted for speech continuation, leaving open questions about the modality-specific requirements of continuous autoregressive modeling.

Objective speaker similarity degradation: In Table 3, objective speaker similarity (SIM) is markedly lower for CALM compared to baselines (0.52 vs. ~0.67), largely inherited from the speech VAE bottleneck itself (0.57 on reference reconstruction).

Several proposed mechanisms, such as the Gaussian temperature sampling heuristic (scaling noise standard deviation by the square root of tau) and latent CFG, are empirical heuristics lacking rigorous theoretical grounding.

Minor presentation and citation defects, notably an unedited bibliography placeholder on page 11 ('Placeholder Author and Various Contributors... Replace with accurate reference if you have one') and missing links in the abstract/introduction.

strengths: Compelling and timely approach: Operates autoregressively over continuous VAE representations while substituting multi-step diffusion/flow heads with 1-to-4-step consistency models, effectively bypassing both the bitrate-computation trade-off of RVQ-based discrete models and the slow inference of prior continuous diffusion heads.

Strong practical efficiency: Achieves notable speedups (up to 12x-20x for the sampling head and ~2x overall) compared to RQ-Transformer baselines, enabling real-time streaming capability and a compact 100M parameter TTS model (Pocket TTS) capable of running faster than real time on standard CPUs.

Comprehensive experimental scope: Unlike prior works that focused narrowly on TTS or short single-instrument stems, this work benchmarks across four challenging tasks: speech continuation, text-to-speech, music continuation, and text-to-music.

Valuable technical contributions: The combination of noise-injected long context with a clean short-context transformer, the head batch multiplier to amortize backbone computation, Gaussian temperature sampling for continuous latents, and latent distillation together form a well-engineered and practical recipe.
Thorough evaluation: Results are backed by both standard objective metrics (FAD, WER, CER, PPX, VERT) and rigorous human perceptual studies (MUSHRA and Bayesian Elo pairwise comparisons).
weaknesses: Task-dependent architectural discrepancies: The dual-transformer design (noisy long context + clean short context) is only used in music continuation; for speech continuation and TTS, it is turned off in favor of text grounding / inner monologue. The paper should more explicitly clarify the distinct failure modes of speech vs. music that dictate these divergent design choices.

Speaker similarity degradation in TTS: As shown in Table 3 and Table 12, the model exhibits lower objective speaker similarity (0.52 vs. 0.66-0.67) and lower human speaker similarity Elo than some baselines (e.g., DSM and Chatterbox Turbo), suggesting that the continuous VAE latent representation or consistency head may slightly compromise voice conditioning fidelity.

Incremental core algorithmic novelty: The overarching framework primarily adapts MAR / continuous-time consistency modeling to audio, although the domain-specific adaptations, system integration, and practical tricks provide solid engineering and empirical value.
Minor presentation issues: Incomplete citation entry for the Emilia dataset ('Placeholder Author and Various Contributors... Replace with accurate reference...').
